title: Waste valorization of  Sterculia foetida  shells into sulfonated carbon catalysts for sustainable biodiesel production from tobacco seed oil
content: The growing demand for renewable energy and environmentally benign catalytic processes has accelerated research on biomass-derived heterogeneous catalysts for biodiesel production. In this study, a novel sulfonated carbon catalyst was synthesized from Sterculia foetida shell biomass and applied to the transesterification of Nicotiana tabacum L. (tobacco) oil for biodiesel production. The catalyst was prepared through thermal carbonization followed by chemical activation and sulfonation, introducing Brønsted acidic (–SO3H) functional groups onto the carbon framework. The physicochemical properties of the catalyst were comprehensively characterized using FTIR, XRD, SEM-EDX, BET, and NMR analyses, confirming the successful incorporation of acidic active sites and the formation of a porous carbon structure. Transesterification parameters, including methanol-to-oil ratio, reaction temperature, catalyst loading, and reaction time, were systematically optimized. The highest biodiesel yield of 95.89% was achieved at a methanol-to-oil ratio of 18 : 1, reaction temperature of 70 °C, catalyst loading of 7 wt% and reaction time of 5 h. The catalyst exhibited excellent catalytic stability and reusability, maintaining high activity over four consecutive cycles with only a minor decline in performance. Product characterization by 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and FTIR spectroscopy and GC confirmed the efficient conversion of triglycerides into fatty acid methyl esters (FAMEs). Economic assessment estimated a biodiesel production cost of approximately USD 3.03 kg−1, indicating promising commercial viability. These findings highlight Sterculia foetida shell waste as a sustainable and low-cost precursor for green catalyst development, supporting biodiesel production, waste valorization, and circular bioeconomy principles.
